claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance and undergoes substantial oxidation and surface degradation in high-temperature air.
A hafnium coating can be deposited on cast HfNbTaTiZr by physical-vapor or spark deposition.
A hafnium coating can chemically bond to the substrate through a compositionally graded transition layer.
Hafnium-rich regions from the coating diffuse into the substrate surface.
The transition layer enables formation of a dense, continuous HfO2 scale.
At high temperature, surface hafnium oxidizes preferentially to form HfO2.
The resulting HfO2 scale is slow-growing and protective.
The HfO2 scale impedes oxygen diffusion into bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
A hafnium coating will significantly reduce oxidation and oxygen uptake relative to uncoated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Reduced oxidation will preserve the alloy's intrinsic room-temperature ductility and high-temperature yield strength.
After oxidation exposure, the coated alloy's ductility and yield strength will remain within the stated untreated-alloy baseline ranges.
The coating is expected to protect HfNbTaTiZr during approximately 5 hours of isothermal exposure in air at about 1000 °C.
The protective coating may remain applicable at temperatures as high as 1600 °C.
In a related VZrHfNbTa alloy, hot-press sintering produced an approximately 120 μm hafnium coating with zirconium diffusion into the coating and a chemically bonded HfZr transition layer.
